findings: The instruction/timing associations use all 12 children in each arm and no fast/slow cutoff.
The report exposes one timed region per sample; it does not expose a decomposable per-stage duration or subphase counter.
The exact report work and output-route signature is stable across all selected children, so the retained report cannot explain child-level timing spread through changing work/output counts.
Perf instructions, cycles, and task-clock are whole-process wrapper counters and should be treated as correlated telemetry rather than an attribution of report-stage cost.

report_structure.selection: all docfloat/e1/default packet children; no timing or counter filter

scope.harness_scope: baseline Instant samples only; excludes wrappers and sidecar I/O
scope.interpretation_limit: descriptive association only; whole-process counters are not decomposed into report stages
scope.selection_policy: all 24 retained Float/e1 children, analyzed separately by arm
scope.timed_region_scope: public Snapshot::open_bounded source clone, one Edit with all paragraph-0 replacements and retention releases, commit, output Vec copy, and local snapshot/edit/commit destruction; source file read, references, correctness checks, hashing and JSON excluded
scope.whole_process_perf_scope: perf measures the launched GNU time command and inherited launcher/baseline process tree; perf bookkeeping is excluded
scope.whole_process_time_scope: launcher startup plus same-PID execed historical baseline

stage_duration_associations.reason: Retained stage records expose before/after/after_release capacities and requested text, but no per-stage duration or counter. All exposed stage/work/output-route values are constant across the 24 selected children.
